title: Nebrakada! Feminimum.
html_source:
“Little heaven of blessed femininity.” This is a curious expression on a number of counts:

First, if (as it first appears) it is Molly angrily scolding the camel the expression makes no sense, which, in this episode, it doesn’t necessarily need to.

Second, the expression is part of a phrase Stephen reads in the Wandering Rocks episode, where he has picked up a book off a barrow in front of Clohissey’s bookshop on Bedford Row. The book purports to contain “Secrets of secrets,” including “How to win a woman’s love.” The full quote is “Se el yilo nebrakada femininum! Amor me solo! Sanktus! Amen,” or “[My] little heaven of blessed femininity, love only me. Holy! Amen.” So this is Bloom’s hallucination, wherein Molly says something neither she nor Bloom knows anything about.

Third, in spite of the fact that it was Molly who had betrayed Bloom earlier in the day, she is demanding, condescending, and angry. It is Bloom whose self-esteem is at low tide (for now). The ludicrous camel “fumbles to kneel” just as Bloom “stoops his back for leapfrog.” The camel is Bloom.
